key_insight: Regularization makes ill-posed inverse problems tractable, while data-driven methods aim to improve reconstructions without sacrificing reliability guarantees.
engineering_relevance: Reliable reconstruction from indirect measurements is essential in applications such as medical imaging, where algorithm-induced artifacts can mislead interpretation.
method: Review classical regularization theory for inverse problems.
Formulate reconstruction as variational optimization and discuss practical algorithms.
Examine unrolling, learned regularizers, and plug-and-play methods alongside their performance guarantees.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a course-style overview, with no datasets, quantitative benchmarks, or experimental results reported.
watch_item: Machine-learning enhancements may reduce explainability or lack convergence guarantees, requiring careful validation of reconstructed features.
